items.text: Test 1 determines whether a material, when exposed to a standard ignition source, will self-extinguish and not transfer burning debris that can ignite adjacent materials.
items.quote: The purpose of this test is to determine if a material, when exposed to a standard ignition source, will self-extinguish and not transfer burning debris, which can ignite adjacent materials.

items.text: Test 1 evaluates the material in the worst-case atmosphere to which it could be exposed; the oxygen level is the highest the material could witness in use.
Five specimens of 30 cm by 6.5 cm, mounted vertically and ignited at the bottom.
A material is self-extinguishing if no specimen burns more than 15 cm and no specimen propagates a flame by transfer of burning debris.
Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC): the maximum oxygen concentration at which at least five specimens pass the acceptance criteria of Test 1.
items.quote: Maximum Oxygen Concentration: The maximum oxygen concentration at which at least five specimens pass the acceptance criteria of this test.

items.text: Air shall not be allowed to flow during tests.

items.text: Fire safety capability areas: (1) fire prevention and material flammability, (2) fire detection, (3) fire suppression, (4) post-fire clean-up.
items.quote: Fire safety is divided into capability areas that include: (1) fire prevention and material flammability, (2) fire detection, (3) fire suppression, and (4) post-fire clean-up.

items.text: Prevention means eliminating one of the three fire-causing factors: fuel, oxygen, ignition energy.
ISS response: after detection, ventilation in the affected module is terminated to slow the spread of fire; a portable CO2 extinguisher is used in the U.S. modules.

items.text: Detectors respond to fire signatures: temperature rise, combustion gases, light and other radiation, particulates (smoke), pressure rise, acoustic waves. Rapid detection with limited false alarms is required.

The rate of buildup of atmospheric gases, particularly carbon monoxide, is an additional early warning; after a fire the module stays isolated until CO, HCN and HCl are reduced to admissible concentrations.

items.text: The extinguishing agent must not support combustion in an O2-enriched environment, contain toxic agents, emit toxic products, interfere with visual observation, or be slow to initiate.

items.quote: Material flammability in partial gravity remains a major gap for exploration missions.

items.text: Carbon monoxide SMAC: 1 hour 425 ppm, 24 hour 100 ppm, 7 day 55 ppm, 30 day 15 ppm, 180 day 15 ppm, 1000 day 15 ppm. Effects: CNS depression, cardiac arrhythmia.

SMACs are based on experiments at standard pressure and oxygen. Rev D applies the published ppm values across all atmospheric scenarios, including reduced-pressure exploration atmospheres, for vapor-phase compounds. 1- and 24-hour values apply to off-nominal situations such as accidental releases. The values were established for human spaceflight and are not intended to apply to other situations such as ground operations.
Pressures listed for unit conversion: 14.7 psia, and 10.2 and 8.2 psia as proposed atmospheres for upcoming missions.

items.text: Recommended nominal atmospheres: 14.7 psia / 21% O2; 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2; 8.0 psia / 32% O2 (landers, surface habitats); 7.6 psia / 32% O2 (surface habitats). Control box +/-0.2 psia and +/-2.0% O2. Recommendations, not requirements.

A white paper appended to the report (Appendix E-2) states that the lander and habitat recommendations require materials ignition and flammability testing and certification to 34% oxygen. items.text: Test 1 is conducted in the most severe environment expected in the spacecraft, currently 30% oxygen at 10.2 psia.

references.title: Flammability Limits from BASS-II Testing in Microgravity Compared to Normal Gravity Limits (Olson, Ferkul, Fernandez-Pello, Miller, Wichman, Bhattacharjee, T'ien)

items.text: The flammability boundary is expressed in oxygen concentration and flow velocity, with a quenching branch at low flow and a blowoff branch at high flow.
Normal ISS ventilation flow velocity range is 5-30 cm/s.
items.quote: the normal ISS ventilation flow velocity range is 5-30 cm/s

items.text: BASS-II PMMA: minimum oxygen concentration in the flammability boundary from the concurrent (stagnation-flow) rod tests 13.6% O2; minimum flammable value for the opposed-flow rods 16.3% O2 (no comparable boundary was obtained for opposed flow); normal-gravity PMMA extinction limits 17% O2 (downward spread) and 15.4% O2 (upward spread).

In BASS-II the flames always quenched when the fan was turned off. The authors call turning off ventilation an excellent mitigation strategy for the ISS, and add that earlier quiescent tests at elevated oxygen suggest ventilation may not be necessary for a flame to survive in high-oxygen low-pressure atmospheres or in partial gravity, so the strategy may not be applicable in future exploration missions.
items.quote: so this mitigation strategy may not be applicable in future exploration missions

references.title: Evaluating Material Flammability in Microgravity and Martian Gravity Compared to the NASA Standard Normal Gravity Test (Olson, Ferkul)

items.text: Oxygen margins of safety (low-gravity limit minus 1g limit, % O2 by mole) were negative by as much as -5.75 (lunar gravity, Mylar G at 10.2 psia); the largest at Martian gravity was -3.35 (Nomex HT90-40) and at 0g -4.1 (Mylar G). Normal-gravity screening tests may not be conservative. The low-g limits come from 5 s drop tests and their extinction criteria are not the same as in 1g.
items.note: The Conclusions sentence of the paper gives 5.75 for Martian gravity; Table I of the same paper gives that value for lunar gravity. The table values are used here.

items.text: Limiting oxygen molar concentrations (% O2) from Table I. Mylar G at 10.2 psia: 1g ULOI 21.2 and MOC 20.0; Martian ULOI* 18.0 and MOC* 17.0; Lunar ULOI* 15.6 and MOC* 14.1; 0g ULOI* 17.0 and MOC* 16.0; oxygen margin of safety (delta O2 %) -3.1 Martian, -5.75 Lunar, -4.1 0g. Ultem 1000 at 10.2 psia: 1g ULOI 23.5 and MOC 23.0; Martian ULOI* 22.0 and MOC* 21.1; Lunar ULOI* 21.0 and MOC* 19.9; 0g ULOI* 24.0 and MOC* 23.0; delta O2 % -1.7 Martian, -2.8 Lunar, 0.25 0g. Nomex HT90-40 at 14.7 psia: 1g ULOI 23.5 and MOC 22.1; Martian ULOI* 19.9 and MOC* 19.0; Lunar ULOI* 21.0 and MOC* 19.9; 0g ULOI* 23.0 and MOC* 22.0; delta O2 % -3.35 Martian, -2.35 Lunar, -0.3 0g. Delta O2 % is the mean of the low-gravity ULOI* and MOC* minus the mean of the 1g ULOI and MOC (Eq. 1). The low-gravity limits come from 5.18 s drop tower tests: MOC* is the maximum oxygen concentration at which the flame self-extinguished during the drop, ULOI* the minimum at which it survived the full drop; these criteria are not the same as in 1g.
items.quote: Table I: Limiting Oxygen Molar Concentrations and Oxygen Margin of Safety for Different Gravity Levels
items.note: The table is printed with one column per fuel and one row per quantity. Column headings as printed: Fuel; Mylar(R) G 10.2 psia; Ultem(R) 1000 10.2 psia; Nomex(R) HT90-40 14.7 psia. Row labels as printed: 1g ULOI, 1g MOC, Martian ULOI*, Martian MOC*, Lunar ULOI*, Lunar MOC*, 0g* ULOI*, 0g* MOC*, Martian delta-O2 %, Lunar delta-O2 %, 0g delta-O2 %. The limit rows carry no unit in the table; the title calls them oxygen molar concentrations. Pressure is printed in psia only (no kPa value in the table). The table has no footnotes: the asterisk on ULOI*/MOC* is defined in the body (p. 4, p. 6), the asterisk on '0g*' is not defined anywhere in the paper; the body says the 0g values were obtained with a concurrent flow of 30 cm/s (p. 4) and that the Lunar and 0g data are from ref. 8 (Ferkul and Olson 2011). The Conclusions (p. 8) attribute 'up to 5.75% O2 lower' to Martian gravity, but in Table I -5.75 is the Lunar value (Mylar G); the largest Martian value in the table is -3.35 (Nomex HT90-40). Read on 2026-11-14 from the NTRS PDF, both from the text layer (pdftotext -layout) and from a 200 dpi rendering of page 6; the two readings agree in every cell. AI-read, not checked by a human.

items.text: Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI): the oxygen mole fraction below which a steady flame cannot exist for a given material and ambient condition. In total flooding, the goal of the agent is to reduce the oxygen concentration below the LOI.
items.quote: For fire safety, the goal of the agent in a total flooding application is to reduce the oxygen concentration below the LOI

items.text: Minimum Extinction Concentration (MEC): the minimum suppressant concentration above which a quasi-steady flame cannot exist. LOI = 0.209 (1 - MEC).

Objectives: map the flammability boundaries for liquid fuel combustion in reduced gravity; quantify the efficacy of gaseous suppressants over the range of candidate atmospheric pressures and O2 concentrations.
